configure.name: configure
configure.title: Load wallet-provider keys, providers, mail sender and back office
configure.description: Provision what the verifier trusts and whom it talks to, then lift the configure-then-freeze gate. Every part is optional on a later call: a part left out keeps its value, so the mail secret need not be resent to change the rest. SHA-256 of the configuration in force, secrets excluded, is attested at OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.65230.5.4.1.

wallet_provider_jwks.description: The wallet-provider keys (privasys.id's) that sign Wallet Instance Attestations. Required on first configuration: every call that does work must carry a WIA bound to the device key that signs it.

providers.description: OIDC providers by name. For google, microsoft and linkedin give {audiences: [privasys.id's client ids]} and, for microsoft, optionally {vouching_tenants: [...]}: issuers, key sets and claim rules are built into the measured image. Any other provider is named oidc:<issuer> and fully defined {issuer, jwks_url, audiences, claims, email_rule}. A null value removes a provider.

mail.description: The Microsoft Graph sender for verification codes: {tenant_id, client_id, client_secret, sender}. The secret stays on the sealed volume and is excluded from the attested digest.

card_check.description: The Privasys back office that answers about card checks: {base_url}. The verifier authenticates with its attested app identity; nothing is configured for that.

tools.name: configure
tools.title: Load wallet-provider keys, providers, mail sender and back office
tools.description: See configure. Returns {status: "configured", configuration_digest, providers, mail, card_check, ledger}.

tools.name: challenge
tools.title: Fresh challenge
tools.description: Returns {challenge, expires_at}: a single-use token, valid two minutes, that every attest and mail_start call must sign.

tools.name: attest
tools.title: Check raw material and sign proofs
tools.description: Wallet only. Checks one piece of raw material against the verifier's trust anchors and returns {proofs: [{attr, value, method, source, label, proof}]}. Kinds: oidc_id_token {provider, id_token, reattest?}; github {access_token}; mail_code {email, code, mail_token}; card_check {check_id, line1, postal_code, country}; proof {proof} (rebind a proof to the calling device). The holder key and the device key both sign canonical JSON {op: "attest", kind, material: base64url(SHA-256(canonical material)), challenge}; a WIA bound to the device key is required.

holder.description: {hk_pub, salt, sig}, base64url: SEC1 holder key, 16-byte salt, raw ES256 signature.

device.description: {pub, sig}, base64url: SEC1 device key, raw ES256 signature.

tools.name: mail_start
tools.title: Mail a verification code
tools.description: Wallet only. Mails a six-digit code to the address and returns {mail_token, expires_at}. Both keys sign canonical JSON {op: "mail_start", email, challenge}. Redeem with attest kind mail_code.

tools.name: disclose
tools.title: Disclose a proof to one app
tools.description: Wallet only. Returns {token}: a short-lived SD-JWT VC of one proof, addressed to rp_id and bound to the device key. The device key signs canonical JSON {op: "disclose", proof: <proof jti>, rp_id, sub, nonce, ts}.

tools.name: status
tools.title: Status
tools.description: Providers configured, whether mail and card checks are available, whether WIA is enforced, and the provider-key ledger's root.
